claims.statement: Every web UI submit carries run_name "chess-web" and tag "web" (WEB_TRACE) plus metadata surface "web", uses multitaskStrategy reject, and puts the game's recorded settings in config.configurable via configurableOf (version first, then every setting key), which lets web traffic be separated from Studio/SDK runs in LangSmith.
The web client's retry sends an empty input to resume a pending turn, because a fresh go would be rejected while a turn is pending; an unanswered first position packet is instead resent unchanged.

chat_model names the chat model after the model part of its spec so gateway LLM spans appear under the model name rather than ChatOpenAI, and caps output at MAX_TOKENS = 64000 including reasoning, lowered to the model's own output limit or half of a smaller context window, with a max_tokens from model_kwargs replacing the budget.
System 1 classifier requests are traced under the run names systemone.rank, systemone.heats and systemone.final.

GatewayRanker retries only transient TypeSafe or OpenAI errors (rate limit, connection/timeout, internal server error), with max_attempts=3 total and backoff_seconds (0.5 s then 1 s) between attempts, and the server's classifiers use the shared pools' HTTP clients with a 15 s timeout, so a request whose attempts all time out blocks for roughly 46.5 s before RankingFailed.

RankingFailed carries the elapsed time and completed calls of the failed ranking, and a skipped System 1 decision stores both, so ply telemetry latency_ms and the turn's latency include time lost to failed rankings.
When ranking fails, a SystemOneMiddleware with has_model=True freezes a skipped decision and the LLM plays unaided, while has_model=False (policy systemone) re-raises RankingFailed and fails the run.

CallRecorder records a Call only when a provider response ends and drops errored provider calls in on_llm_error, so a turn's recorded calls undercount failed or stalled attempts that traces still show.

turn.latency_ms is the wall time inside ChessCore.wrap_model_call plus each extension's turn_latency_ms (System 1 ranking, counted once across retries), folded in when the turn finalizes or is abandoned; it excludes summarization and graph overhead, so it is lower than root-trace latency.

Each illegal or unparseable reply triggers feedback and another model call while illegal_attempts < max_retries (default 3); after that a resignation terminal_intent with reason illegal_moves is set. The counter lives on the durable turn record, so a resume after a provider error keeps the remaining budget and a turn gets at most four parsed replies.

wrap_model_call runs the provider call inside provider_errors(), which re-raises exceptions that look like context overflow as ContextBudgetError, including when the overflow follows a completed call, leaving the turn pending.

ChessContext (settings version 3) defaults are policy hybrid, model langsmith:baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash with no reasoning_effort and empty model_kwargs, memory off, threshold 0.9 with the margin gate, tournament_threshold unset, k 5, systemone_model typesafe/jev-latest, and with_eval and with_nouls off; the version-3 migration replaces retired semif- System 1 models with Jev.

The UCI adapter answers a committed ply with its move, a resignation, other game end or rejected position with bestmove 0000 plus info strings, and after a cancellation or failure plays System 1's fallback_move only if this search's turn left one inside the root pool, otherwise forfeiting with 0000; it never plays a random move.

resolve_context migrates the assistant context and then config configurable to the current settings version (dropping unknown keys and reading a source without version as current), merges them with the later source winning, treats an explicit null as a reset to the default, and validates the merged values with ChessContext so a bad setting fails the run up front.

With memory on, summarization triggers at 70% of the model's input limit; gateway models get a profile with max_input_tokens equal to the known context window minus the output budget, and build_agent raises ChessContractError when the model has no known input limit.

policy systemone builds no chat model, so memory is ignored, and sets both System 1 thresholds to 0 with has_model=False so System 1 always plays, while policy llm with fixed_topology (as on the server) installs the no-op NoSystemOne placeholder that keeps the node but ranks nothing.

On the server an openai/ systemone_model uses OpenAI Decisions with LANGSMITH_GATEWAY credentials, while any other System 1 model needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY and TYPESAFE_BASE_URL (ValueError when missing, raised while building the ranker); a gateway or TypeSafe variable that is set but blank is rejected rather than treated as unset.

When a model call records a completed response and then fails, wrap_model_call keeps the completed calls on the turn and writes a failed_call marker; after_model re-raises the original error in the same run, and because the error is held only in instance memory, a later resume clears the marker and calls the model again.

An empty-input resume of a pending turn finalizes an already validated proposal or terminal intent without calling the model again; otherwise it clears the decision fields and restores allowed_moves from the turn's initial_allowed. A new chat message while a turn is pending is rejected, and a new position request abandons the pending turn.

System 1 HTTP clients come from two per-process ClientPools with a 15 s timeout (POOL with httpx2 clients for TypeSafe, DECISIONS_POOL with httpx clients for OpenAI Decisions), each created lazily under a lock so concurrent first uses make one pair, kept in clients.py because langgraph loads graph.py under a generated module name; the FastAPI lifespan, merged with the Agent Server's, closes both on shutdown and the next get creates a fresh pair.

The web table shows a ChessCore rejection (state error) as a dismissible "Move rejected" banner, a failed run or submit as an inline error message, a 401/403 from the Agent Server as an API-key banner, silently drops a busy-run rejection, and for a pending turn locks the board and offers a Retry button instead of asking the opponent to move.

The web new-game dialog asks GET /ui/model, which returns max_input_tokens from the cached model_limit and takes_effort; it offers memory only for a known input limit and sends no reasoning effort to a model known to take none, and a failed request is treated as knowing nothing.

When the Agent Server calls the graph factory without an execution runtime (state reads, updates, introspection), make_graph returns a shape graph with every node switched off that needs no model, clients or credentials.

StallRetry retries only a stalled response stream (langchain_openai StreamChunkTimeoutError, or nothing when langchain_openai is absent) once, with no delay and on_failure error, inside the same turn; a second stall re-raises so the run fails with the turn pending for Retry.

StallRetry is appended last in the stack while ChessCore is first with the outermost wrap_model_call, so StallRetry runs inside ChessCore.wrap_model_call: the time spent on a stalled attempt counts toward turn.latency_ms while the stalled attempt itself records no Call.
CallRecorder marks a recorded call cost_complete False when its request carried hosted tools, because token prices do not cover those tools' own charges.

The server builds the chat model with surface server, which accepts only an allowlist of request arguments from model_kwargs and holds back account resources such as hosted tools, and the graph's run metadata records the values actually sent.

A provider 400 about the reasoning effort (param reasoning.effort or reasoning_effort, or a message mentioning effort when no param is given) is re-raised from model and summary calls as ReasoningEffortError with advice to remove the effort, and the turn stays pending.

chat_model raises ModelArgumentsError at construction for a reasoning_effort on a model the effort catalog says takes none, and for an output limit that fills the model's context window, so these fail before the first provider call.

A resign command is handled before the pending-turn rejection, so it abandons a pending turn without playing its saved decision and ends the game, while a draw offer during a pending turn is rejected; the web keeps Resign available but disables draw offers while a turn is pending.

The web client sends moves, go, resign and draw as chat messages whose ids are fixed per (ply, content) within a game, so a resend is a server no-op, and a game from a custom root starts with one position packet that Retry resends unchanged until the root is accepted.

systemone_model selects the System 1 client: openai/<model> is OpenAI Decisions wrapped in DecisionsClassifier with the OpenAI client's own retries disabled, anything else TypeSafe, and retries, validation, tournaments and tracing stay in GatewayRanker for both; a Decisions refusal is dropped and read as a malformed answer.
A System 1 tournament happens only when the legal moves exceed the model's per-request cap, which is 255 for typesafe/jev- and openai/ models and 16 for other classifiers.

System 1 calls are priced from reported usage: OpenAI Decisions calls at the repository's per-token Decisions rate on input tokens, Jev through genai-prices under typesafe, and any other classifier or a call without usage gets cost_usd None.
